tasks.notes: Sibling-path overlap on `AGENTS.md`. The diff edits `AGENTS.md` (the new `__TINYAPP_SYNC__` bullet in `## Key Files`, patch lines 9-15), which this task's own Files block declares as `Modify:` and which M5 plus the first Proof `Run:` line require — but `AGENTS.md` is also listed under SIBLING FILES group 4 (popmechanic-tinyapp-fixture#7n6t). Both tasks therefore append to the same `## Key Files` list, so the two branches will collide on integration. The implementer could not have avoided this without abandoning M5; the fix is in the plan's file assignment, not in this tree. Nothing else in the diff leaves this task's FILES (`client/src/config.ts`, `client/src/Store.tsx`, `client/src/storeData.ts`, `client/src/vite-env.d.ts`, `client/test/sync-origin.test.ts` are all declared), no BASE file is deleted, and no other sibling-owned path is touched.; unverified: GLOBAL CONSTRAINT "No exam dials anything but loopback" is not settled by this diff. `readSyncOrigin` (client/src/storeData.ts) accepts any `ws://`/`wss://` string — exactly what M1 specifies — so the origin is scheme-checked but not host-checked; a harness handing in `ws://example.com` would be dialled. Enforcement of the loopback-only rule lives in the browser-side request block owned by sibling group 3 (`packages/tinyapp-exam/src/browser.ts`), which this patch does not touch. What would settle it: the sibling's block failing every non-127.0.0.1 request before it leaves the machine, exercised against a page carrying a non-loopback `__TINYAPP_SYNC__`.

Proof leg (d) requires that `events(cb)` followed by `fork('todos','todos@y')` deliver "a transition whose `module` is `todos@y` and whose `seq` is a number". The exam at packages/tinyapp-exam/test/celld.test.ts does not pin the `module` half: its header paragraph declares the clause "not satisfiable against the server as at BASE" and returns it "under `unsatisfiable`", and the test body asserts only `expect(typeof t.module).toBe('string')` with the wait loop keyed on `seen.length === 0`. That declaration is contradicted by the submission's own first AMENDMENTS entry, which says `examSurface.fork` now dials `<ws>/sync/<to>` and hangs up before fetching `/exam/fork` precisely so the module object learns its name, and that "after it, the seed transition reads `{module:'todos@y',seq:2}`" — and the diff does carry that dial (packages/tinyapp-exam/src/surface.ts, `prime`). So the amendment's whole justification is a leg the exam then refuses to read: the named clause of leg (d) has no evidence anywhere in the submission, and the amendment's `why` is itself unverified. Pin the clause — wait for, and assert, a transition whose `module` is `todos@y` — and drop the stale "unsatisfiable" paragraph. (Assert over the forked subset rather than over every message in `seen`, since transitions of other modules may also arrive on the socket.) EXAM EVIDENCE shows the file green, so the fix is a strengthening of a green exam, not a repair of a red one.
